title: Unified Performance Briefing Panel — compact per-model & per-route telemetry
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design a compact, skimmable 'Performance Briefing Panel' for the Redwood Console that unifies per-model and per-route telemetry into a single slide-in panel and a lightweight route tile. The panel's goals are: 1) let engineers and SREs quickly assess latency, throughput, and token cost health for a route or model; 2) compare model variants (quantized vs full-precision) and recent rollouts; 3) surface actionable anomalies and suggested mitigations (scale, fallback, cache). This ticket captures the prototype screens, chart encoding rules, trade-offs, and review feedback needed to move to engineering handoff.
chart_specs: Latency corridor (p50/p90/p99) — stacked area with corridor shading; aggregation: 1m for >12h range, 10s for <1h; y-axis linear ms; tooltip shows raw percentile values and sample size; color tokens: primary-500 for p50, amber-500 for p90, red-600 for p99.

Throughput sparkline + burst overlay — line for req/s, faint band for 95th percentile burst; heatmap layer beneath for concurrency density (time vs concurrency buckets); aggregation: 10s sampling; recommended min-height 48px in compact tile.

Token flow waterfall — stacked bars per request bucket showing prompt tokens, generated tokens, and cached hits; bars normalized to average request to show cost mix; hover expands to distribution histogram and recent example prompts (anonymized).

Cost attribution donut (micro) — token-based cost breakdown by model variant + accelerator (e.g., a100 vs t4); slice labels hidden at <6% and exposed in tooltip; supports toggles to show token vs GPU-time cost bases.
Model-compare lane — small multiples of latency corridors for up to 4 variants aligned on the same time axis; synchronized hover and rollouts overlay (canary % band).
Anomaly timeline — vertical markers for incidents, deploys, and rollout steps; markers colored by type and tappable to surface linked changelogs/PRs.
Error-rate tiny-bar — compact stacked bar for 4xx vs 5xx with trend arrow and micro-legend; shown in tile when >0.1% error rate.
Latency distribution violin (detail view) — shows percentile density; recommended in detailed panel only (not tile) due to complexity.
Sampling rules — default dashboard sampling at 1:100 for raw token-level traces, adaptive sampling up to 1:1 during incidents; UI exposes sampling snapshot with 'inspect sample' button.

Color, thresholds, and alerts mapping — use semantic tokens: ok (green-500), warning (amber-500), critical (red-600); thresholds set by route with recommended defaults based on model family and seq-length.
ux_notes: Primary entry: route > 'Performance' quick action or model catalog > 'Briefing' button opens sliding panel anchored to right.
Compact route tile (60–120px height) shows 3 micro-widgets: small latency corridor, throughput sparkline, and cost micro-donut with single-digit percentage overlay.
Compare mode: users can pin up to 4 model variants side-by-side; pin state persists to workspace and is shareable via link.
Rollout overlay: show canary % as a translucent band on the time axis; tooltip includes rollout name, start/end, and target traffic percent.
Interaction: hover/tap synchronizes across charts; keyboard navigation supports move focus between micro-widgets and expand to detail using Enter.
Mobile: provide stacked vertical layout and simplified charts (no small-multiples) with critical metrics only: p90 latency, rps, token-cost per 1k requests.
Accessibility: ensure contrast ratios for small lines; offer high-contrast mode and numeric fallback badges for each metric for screen-reader consumption.
Data granularity control: top-right control allows selecting time window (15m, 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d) and aggregation granularity.
Permutations: tile vs panel vs full screen—design tokens define min and max chart sizes to preserve readability; micro-widgets collapse when width < 320px.
Annotations: allow engineers to pin investigation notes tied to time ranges; those notes appear as table rows exportable to CSV.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: default to p90 for single-number health indicator in tiles because p99 is too noisy for quick triage; retain p99 in the detailed panel.
Trade-off: small-multiples improve comparison but add rendering cost and layout complexity—limit to 4 columns and provide server-side image fallback for heavy workloads.
Decision: show cost as token-cost by default; allow toggle to GPU-time for dedicated customers who care about hardware billing.
Trade-off: animated transitions improve comprehension but can mask transient spikes; animations limited to crossfades and subtle band movement, disabled during live incident mode.
Decision: sampling settings are surfaced but default to conservative sampling to reduce storage cost; during incidents, sampling escalates automatically.
Security note: no raw prompt text is exposed by default; examples must be anonymized and flagged in audit logs.

acceptance_criteria: Compact tile available in route list showing p90 latency, rps sparkline, and cost micro-donut.
Slide-in Briefing Panel shows latency corridor (p50/p90/p99), throughput heatmap, token waterfall, cost attribution, and rollout overlay.
Model-compare mode supports up to 4 pinned variants with synchronized hover and rollout bands.
Mitigation quick-actions present and wired to placeholder API endpoints for engineering integration testing.
Design tokens, color mappings, and chart encoding rules documented in the handoff artifact.
Accessibility checklist completed (keyboard, screen reader, contrast) and verified by QA.
Performance: heatmap rendering must not increase page load TTFB by >200ms for default 24h window (engineering measurement).
Privacy: no raw prompt text displayed; example prompts anonymized and logged.
